papers.title: Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common, life-threatening complication among hospitalized patients. Timely prediction is crucial for prevention, while accurate prognosis following onset is essential for guiding care. Although electronic health records (EHRs) provide rich longitudinal data, their high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity pose challenges for traditional machine learning.
papers.summary: This retrospective multicenter study develops a biomarker-aware transformer model that leverages longitudinal electronic health record data to predict both the onset of acute kidney injury and its subsequent prognosis. The approach addresses the high dimensionality and temporal complexity of EHR data, aiming to support earlier prevention and better post-onset care decisions. The abstract does not report specific performance results, so the empirical gains remain to be evaluated.

papers.title: PanRes: A database of latent and acquired antimicrobial resistance allowing 3D-based protein homology search.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance databases are central to genomic surveillance, but resistance determinants remain distributed across resources with different scopes, structures, and annotations.
papers.summary: PanRes is a new database that consolidates antimicrobial resistance determinants from multiple sources into a single resource, including both latent and acquired resistance genes. It enables 3D-based protein homology searches, allowing researchers to identify resistance proteins by structural similarity even when sequence similarity is low. This integrated approach improves genomic surveillance and discovery of resistance mechanisms.

papers.title: An Ontology for Workplace Violence: Protocol to Support Cross-Sector Incident Reporting in Public Services.
papers.abstract: Underreporting is a defining problem in the documentation of workplace violence across public services. This is reinforced by inconsistent, often poor incident descriptions and the absence of a clear, shared nomenclature. Without an ontology-backed structure, similar events are recorded differently across settings or remain uncodable and effectively invisible. Moreover, workplace violence (WPV) is typically registered and studied within sector- and even organization-specific categories and local reporting logics rather than through a shared semantic framework, limiting comparability and cumula
papers.summary: This protocol paper proposes developing a shared ontology for workplace violence (WPV) incident reporting across public services, addressing the problem of underreporting caused by inconsistent terminology and sector-specific reporting logics. The ontology aims to provide a common semantic framework so that similar events can be recorded comparably across settings, enabling cumulative analysis. The paper describes the planned methodology rather than reporting completed results.

papers.title: EBV-HSA-RegDB: A database of regulatory interactions between Epstein-Barr virus and human miRNAs.
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a ubiquitous human herpesvirus associated with various malignancies and autoimmune diseases. MiRNAs play crucial roles in viral-host interactions by regulating gene expression post-transcriptionally. Understanding the regulatory networks between EBV-encoded miRNAs and human miRNAs is essential for elucidating viral pathogenesis and identifying therapeutic targets. We reported the EBV-HSA miRNA Regulatory Database (EBV-HSA-RegDB, https://lbcd.ufpa.br/ebvhsa or  https://lbcd.ia.br/ebvhsa ), an integrated bioinformatics resource that combines comparative sequence analy
papers.summary: This paper presents EBV-HSA-RegDB, a curated database of regulatory interactions between Epstein-Barr virus-encoded miRNAs and human miRNAs, built by integrating comparative sequence analysis with other bioinformatics approaches. The resource aims to help researchers map the viral-host miRNA regulatory network underlying EBV pathogenesis and identify potential therapeutic targets. It is a specialized, web-accessible database rather than a new experimental finding.

papers.title: Comparative Toxicity of Antifouling Paint Particle Suspensions and Dissolved Leachates in the Marine Copepod Tigriopus japonicus.
papers.abstract: Antifouling paint particles (APPs), generated by coating degradation and ship-maintenance activities, are an emerging but poorly characterized source of marine pollution. APPs can release particle-associated and dissolved toxicants, yet their relative contributions to toxicity remain unclear. In this study, environmentally collected APPs were used to prepare two exposure media: an APP suspension containing suspended paint particles and dissolved constituents, and a corresponding membrane-filtered leachate representing the operationally defined dissolved fraction. Their toxic effects on the mar
papers.summary: This study compares the toxicity of suspended antifouling paint particles versus their dissolved leachates in the marine copepod Tigriopus japonicus, using environmentally collected particles. It aims to disentangle how much toxicity comes from the particles themselves versus dissolved toxicants released from them. The work addresses an understudied pollution source from ship coatings and maintenance.

papers.title: Unlocking the full potential of spatial omics in plants: practical challenges, solutions, and a path forward.
papers.abstract: Spatial omics technologies provide new opportunities for plant biology by enabling molecular profiling within structurally intact tissues, revealing spatially organized cell states, developmental gradients, and regulatory interactions. While spatial transcriptomics has driven early advances, the field is rapidly expanding toward integrated spatial multi-omics by combining single-cell and spatial transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data. These approaches offer new opportunities to study development, physiology, and plant biotic and abiotic interactions in spatially preserved
papers.summary: This perspective reviews how spatial omics technologies can be applied to plant biology, moving beyond spatial transcriptomics toward integrated multi-omics that combines single-cell and spatial data across transcriptomes, epigenomes, proteomes, and metabolomes. The authors outline practical challenges specific to plant tissues—such as cell walls, autofluorescence, and large tissue sizes—and propose solutions and a roadmap for the field. The paper is a practical guide for plant researchers adopting these methods.

papers.title: Dermatopathology 2030: Navigating the Digital, Computational and Molecular Convergence for Precision Diagnostics-Originated from a Round Table Discussion at A 66, Basel.
papers.abstract: Background: Traditional dermatopathology relies on analog, qualitative pattern recognition, which encounters critical limitations when facing diagnostic "gray zones" and ambiguous tumor proliferations. Objectives: This paper synthesizes a comprehensive framework integrating Whole Slide Imaging (WSI), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and multi-omics to evaluate how this structural convergence redesigns diagnostic risk and safety ecosystems toward 2030. Methods: We analyze the conceptual shift from individual microscope-based observation to multiple data integration. We integrate recent algorithmic
papers.summary: This perspective piece synthesizes a round-table discussion on how dermatopathology is shifting from analog microscope-based pattern recognition to an integrated digital workflow combining whole-slide imaging, artificial intelligence, and multi-omics. The authors argue that this convergence can resolve diagnostic gray zones and ambiguous tumor proliferations, and they outline a framework for redesigning diagnostic risk and safety ecosystems toward 2030. It is a conceptual/roadmap paper rather than a primary study with new data.

papers.title: MTB-KB: A Curated Knowledgebase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Related Studies.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), has regained its position as the world's leading killer among infectious diseases. Despite extensive research progress across epidemiology, diagnosis, drug development, treatment regimens, vaccines, drug resistance, virulence factors, and immune mechanisms, MTB-related knowledge remains fragmented across thousands of publications, limiting its application in research and clinical practice. To address this gap, we present MTB-KB, a literature-curated knowledgebase that systematically integrates high-impact findings from eight major
papers.summary: MTB-KB is a literature-curated knowledgebase that systematically integrates high-impact findings on Mycobacterium tuberculosis from eight major research areas, including epidemiology, diagnosis, drug development, treatment, vaccines, drug resistance, virulence factors, and immune mechanisms. It addresses the fragmentation of TB knowledge across thousands of publications, aiming to make this information more accessible for research and clinical practice.

papers.title: DHX15 as a novel immune-related prognostic biomarker in breast cancer: An integrated bioinformatics analysis with in vitro functional validation.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is a disease that occurs relatively frequently, and its prognosis and treatment outcomes are not optimal at present. Identifying novel BC biomarkers and therapeutic targets is key. DEAH-box helicase 15 (DHX15) is an RNA helicase that exhibits enhanced activity and is closely associated with tumorigenic potential. Alternative splicing is widely dysregulated in BC. However, the biological function of DHX15 in BC, in addition to its underlying molecular mechanisms, remain unclear. DHX15, a key RNA helicase involved in splicing regulation, was therefore selected to explore wheth
papers.summary: This study identifies the RNA helicase DHX15 as a potential immune-related prognostic biomarker in breast cancer using integrated bioinformatics analysis, and supports the finding with in vitro functional experiments. The work links DHX15 expression to alternative splicing regulation and immune features in breast cancer, suggesting it may serve as both a prognostic marker and a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Methods for determining indications for antibiotic prescriptions to facilitate antimicrobial stewardship: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Effective antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) requires accurate information on the reason for prescribing antimicrobials. To design targeted interventions aimed at improving guideline adherence, accurate information on the indication for each prescription is necessary. This scoping review maps the existing methods used for systematically determining indications for antibiotic prescriptions.
papers.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
papers.summary: This scoping review maps methods for systematically determining the indication for antibiotic prescriptions, a prerequisite for targeted antimicrobial stewardship. It catalogs existing approaches and highlights gaps, providing a foundation for designing interventions to improve guideline adherence.

papers.title: Digital Twins in Oncology: From Multimodal Data Integration to Precision Clinical Practice.
papers.abstract: Oncology digital twins are patient-specific computational models that are built by combining electronic health records, multiomics genomic data, and diagnostic imaging to simulate individual tumor biology and predict multiple treatment-related outcomes. Conceptually originated from aerospace engineering, it has matured clinically through convergent advances in radiomics, mechanistic tumor modeling, pharmacokinetic- pharmacodynamic systems, federated machine learning, and, most recently, large language model (LLM)-based clinical interfaces and agentic artificial intelligence (AI). For a practic
papers.journal: The Indian journal of radiology & imaging
papers.summary: This review describes oncology digital twins—patient-specific computational models that integrate electronic health records, multiomics data, and diagnostic imaging to simulate individual tumor biology and predict treatment outcomes. It traces the concept from aerospace engineering to clinical maturity through radiomics, mechanistic tumor modeling, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic systems, federated machine learning, and emerging LLM-based and agentic AI interfaces. The paper frames these technologies as converging toward precision clinical practice in oncology.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis of extracellular vesicle cargo in cancer.
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are increasingly recognized as minimally invasive sources of molecular information in cancer, carrying nucleic acids, proteins, lipids, and metabolites that reflect tumor biology. Recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and mass spectrometry have not only enabled multi-omics profiling of EV cargo but also revealed that different molecular layers capture distinct yet complementary aspects of cancer processes. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the rapidly expanding landscape of EV multi-omics, highlighting methodological constraints, the predomin
papers.summary: This review surveys how extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry nucleic acids, proteins, lipids, and metabolites that reflect tumor biology, and how high-throughput sequencing and mass spectrometry now allow multi-omics profiling of this cargo. It emphasizes that different molecular layers capture complementary aspects of cancer processes, and discusses methodological constraints and the potential of EV multi-omics for minimally invasive cancer diagnostics.

papers.title: HuRInterDB: A Database Exploring the Landscape of lncRNA-Protein Interactions.
papers.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) possess diverse biological functions and play key regulatory roles in biological processes by interacting with other biomolecules, such as proteins, RNAs, and the genome. High-throughput RNA-interaction experiments have generated large volumes of lncRNA-protein interaction records. The fragmented deposition of these records across disparate public databases complicates unified retrieval and integrative analysis. Here, we present HuRInterDB (Human lncRNA-Protein Interaction Database), a comprehensive and standardized database that focuses on human lncRNA-protein in
papers.summary: HuRInterDB is a new comprehensive database that consolidates human lncRNA-protein interaction data from multiple public sources into a standardized, unified resource. It addresses the fragmentation of interaction records across disparate databases, enabling easier retrieval and integrative analysis of lncRNA-protein interactions.

papers.title: ICD-11 and diabetes: opportunities for precision public health through enhanced classification.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus poses a major global health challenge, yet its intrinsic heterogeneity has been poorly captured by traditional classification systems. The international classification of diseases, tenth revision (ICD-10), built on a phenotype-based framework, lacks the granularity needed to incorporate contemporary molecular insights into diabetes subtypes, hampering both clinical precision and public health surveillance.
papers.summary: This paper argues that ICD-10's phenotype-based diabetes classification is too coarse to capture the disease's molecular and clinical heterogeneity, limiting both precision medicine and public health surveillance. It proposes that ICD-11's expanded classification offers opportunities to integrate contemporary molecular insights into diabetes subtypes, enabling more precise public health strategies.

papers.title: IMicAP: an intelligent microbial application platform for knowledge-driven microbiome research.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms play a pivotal role in health and disease, yet microbial research is hindered by fragmented data, heterogeneous knowledge representation, and a lack of integrated analytical tools. Existing databases and knowledge graphs often focus narrowly on genomic information, leaving critical metabolomic and literature-based associations underdeveloped.
papers.summary: IMicAP is presented as an integrated platform for knowledge-driven microbiome research, designed to address fragmented microbial data, heterogeneous knowledge representation, and the lack of unified analytical tools. It aims to combine genomic, metabolomic, and literature-based associations that existing databases and knowledge graphs typically underdevelop.

papers.title: Microbiota-derived metabolite signatures in Alzheimer's disease across the cognitive aging continuum: a human-focused systematic review and evidence-weighted knowledge graph.
papers.abstract: Gut microbial metabolism is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), preclinical amyloid accumulation, and cognitive aging. However, existing reviews often focus on microbial taxonomy rather than the metabolite mediators that connect the gut ecosystem with AD pathology, neuroinflammation, and cognition.
papers.summary: This systematic review shifts focus from microbial taxonomy to the metabolite mediators linking gut microbial metabolism with Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, preclinical amyloid accumulation, and cognitive aging. The authors synthesize human evidence across the cognitive aging continuum and integrate it into an evidence-weighted knowledge graph, providing a structured resource for understanding which microbiota-derived metabolites are most robustly associated with AD-related outcomes.

papers.title: CfDNA methylation profiling in blood following moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury using brain cell type-enriched signatures: A pilot study.
papers.abstract: The human brain consists of diverse cell types that collaboratively perform complex functions and form intricate neuronal networks. When traumatic brain injury (TBI) occurs, multiple molecular pathways involving diverse cell types are activated in response to injury. Understanding how brain cell composition is altered during TBI may help improve patient outcomes. Upon brain trauma, neurovascular disruption leads to the release of brain-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) into peripheral blood. The tissue-specific DNA methylation patterns in this cfDNA have the potential to serve as candidate markers
papers.summary: This pilot study used brain cell type-enriched DNA methylation signatures to profile cell-free DNA in blood from patients with moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury. The authors show that brain-derived cfDNA with cell-type-specific methylation patterns can be detected in peripheral blood after trauma, suggesting a potential non-invasive way to monitor brain cell composition changes following TBI. As a pilot, the findings are preliminary and need validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: How AI-based techniques for brain tumour diagnosis can address data variability.
papers.abstract: Data variability in medical imaging of tumors refers to the inconsistencies in Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Computational Tomography scans caused by heterogeneous tumor biology, varying scanner hardware, and subjective human interpretation. This variability creates significant challenges for accurate diagnoses, treatment tracking, and AI model development. Although the variability in medical imaging data for diagnostic and prognostic purposes is a challenge for AI methods applied to other types of tumors as well, it is particularly problematic when the analysis involves gliomas and glioblast
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses how data variability in brain tumour imaging—arising from heterogeneous tumour biology, differing scanner hardware, and subjective human interpretation—poses major challenges for AI-based diagnosis, particularly for gliomas and glioblastomas. The authors argue that AI techniques can be designed or adapted to address this variability, improving diagnostic accuracy and treatment tracking.
